chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Nu'aym ibn Ibrahim, from Misma' Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

Regarding four men who testified against a woman for adultery, one of whom was her husband, he عليه السلام said: “The three are to be flogged, and her husband is to engage in li'an with her. They are to be separated, and she is never lawful for him again.”

key_terms.الْفُجُورِ: adultery or illicit sexual misconduct in this legal context
key_terms.لَا تَحِلُّ: she is not lawful for him
key_terms.يُجْلَدُونَ: they are to be flogged as a prescribed legal punishment
key_terms.يُفَرَّقُ: they are to be separated in marriage
key_terms.يُلَاعِنُهَا: he performs li'an with her, invoking mutual imprecation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband is one of four witnesses accusing his wife of adultery?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a case in which four testify against a woman for adultery and one of them is her husband. It states that the three non-husband witnesses receive the hadd for false accusation, while the husband proceeds through li'an, after which the spouses are separated permanently.
